topics.title: Vectors
topics.description: Geometric and algebraic representation of vectors in 2D and 3D space.
objectives: Represent vectors geometrically and as coordinate tuples
Perform vector addition, scalar multiplication
Compute dot product and cross product
Understand magnitude, direction, and unit vectors

problem_templates.prompt_template: Given vectors u = (2, −1, 3) and v = (−1, 4, 2), compute u·v, |u|, and the unit vector in the direction of u. Show each formula.
Compute u × v for u = (1, 2, 0) and v = (3, 0, −1). Verify that the result is orthogonal to both u and v using the dot product.
Find the projection of w = (4, 1, −2) onto the plane spanned by u = (1, 0, 1) and v = (0, 1, 1). Use the Gram-Schmidt process to find an orthogonal basis first.

topics.title: Matrices
topics.description: Rectangular arrays of numbers representing linear transformations and systems.
objectives: Define matrices and their dimensions
Add and subtract matrices
Understand matrix as a linear transformation
Compute transpose and recognize special matrices

problem_templates.prompt_template: Given A = [[1,2],[3,4]] and B = [[5,0],[−1,2]], compute A + B, A − B, and 3A. State the dimensions of each result.
Interpret the matrix T = [[0,−1],[1,0]] as a geometric transformation in ℝ². Apply T to the points (1,0), (0,1), and (1,1). Describe the transformation.

topics.title: Matrix Operations
topics.description: Multiplication, inversion, and determinants of matrices.
objectives: Multiply matrices and understand non-commutativity
Compute the determinant of 2×2 and 3×3 matrices
Find the inverse of a matrix when it exists
Apply properties of determinants

problem_templates.prompt_template: Compute det(A) for A = [[2,1,0],[1,3,1],[0,1,2]] using cofactor expansion along the first row. Show each minor.
Find A⁻¹ for A = [[3,1],[5,2]] using the adjugate formula. Verify by computing A·A⁻¹.
Show that AB ≠ BA in general by constructing a counterexample with 2×2 matrices. Then find two non-trivial matrices that do commute and explain why.

topics.title: Linear Systems
topics.description: Solving systems of linear equations via Gaussian elimination and matrix methods.
objectives: Write a linear system in matrix form Ax=b
Apply row reduction and Gaussian elimination
Determine consistency and the solution set
Understand the geometric interpretation of solutions

problem_templates.prompt_template: Solve the system: x + 2y − z = 3, 2x − y + z = 1, −x + y + 2z = 4. Use Gaussian elimination with full row operations shown.
Determine for which values of k the system x + y = 2, x + ky = k has (a) a unique solution, (b) no solution, (c) infinitely many solutions. Interpret geometrically.
Find the complete solution to Ax = b where A = [[1,2,0,1],[0,0,1,2]] and b = [[3],[4]]. Express as x_p + N(A) in parametric form.

topics.title: Determinants
topics.description: Scalar values encoding volume scaling, orientation, and invertibility of a matrix.
objectives: Compute determinants via cofactor expansion and row operations
Apply properties: multilinearity, antisymmetry, det(AB)=det(A)det(B)
Relate det(A)=0 to singular matrices and the null space
Use Cramer's rule for small linear systems

problem_templates.prompt_template: Compute det(A) for A = [[3,1,2],[0,−1,4],[2,0,1]] using cofactor expansion along the first column. Show each 2×2 minor.
Use properties of the determinant to evaluate det([[1,a,a²],[1,b,b²],[1,c,c²]]) (Vandermonde matrix). Factor the result completely.
Prove that if A is an n×n matrix with two identical rows, det(A)=0. Then use Cramer's rule to solve 2x+y=5, x−y=1.

topics.title: Eigenvalues and Eigenvectors
topics.description: Special scalars and vectors that reveal intrinsic properties of linear transformations.
objectives: Define eigenvalues and eigenvectors
Compute eigenvalues from the characteristic equation
Find eigenvectors for each eigenvalue
Apply spectral decomposition and PCA intuition

problem_templates.prompt_template: Find all eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [[4,1],[2,3]]. Show the characteristic polynomial and solve for each eigenspace.
Find all eigenvalues and eigenvectors of A = [[1,2,0],[0,3,4],[0,0,2]]. Identify any repeated eigenvalues and describe their eigenspaces.
Explain the geometric meaning of eigenvalues and eigenvectors for the matrix [[2,0],[0,3]] acting on ℝ². Then use this to compute A¹⁰ efficiently.

topics.title: Vector Spaces
topics.description: Abstract generalization of vectors — sets closed under addition and scalar multiplication.
objectives: State the axioms of a vector space
Identify subspaces, span, and linear independence
Define basis and dimension
Understand null space and column space of a matrix

problem_templates.prompt_template: Determine whether S = {(x,y,z) : x + y = 0} is a subspace of ℝ³. Check all three subspace conditions and give counterexamples if any fail.
Find a basis for the null space of A = [[1,2,−1,0],[2,4,0,1],[−1,−2,1,0]]. State the nullity and rank, and verify the rank-nullity theorem.
Show that {1, x, x²} is a basis for P₂ (polynomials of degree ≤ 2). Then find the coordinates of p(x) = 3 − 2x + x² in this basis.

topics.title: Diagonalization
topics.description: Decomposing a matrix as PDP⁻¹ to simplify powers, exponentials, and dynamical systems.
objectives: Determine when a matrix is diagonalizable
Construct P and D from eigenvectors and eigenvalues
Compute matrix powers efficiently via A^k = PD^kP⁻¹
Apply to discrete dynamical systems and Markov chains

problem_templates.prompt_template: Diagonalize A = [[3,1],[0,2]] by finding P and D such that A = PDP⁻¹. Verify by computing PDP⁻¹ explicitly.
Use diagonalization to compute A⁶ for A = [[2,1],[0,3]]. Compare the work to six direct matrix multiplications.
Determine whether B = [[2,1,0],[0,2,1],[0,0,2]] is diagonalizable. If not, explain why and describe its Jordan form instead.
